I still have non-Brazilian friends who think São Paulo is fine to visit

We hired a great Uber driver to drive us to Florianopolis, like a 3 hour trip, cause was easier than flying then, very nice guy

While driving I sat in the back talking a bit with him and practicing my Portuguese

Then I noticed he didn't wear a seatbelt so I asked why

He said "so I can draw my gun quickly"

I said "desculpa the fuck what gun"

Then he showed he was wearing a holster on his right side with a gun it which he carried for safety because he said drive into and out of São Paulo often

So being a funny naive Dutch guy I asked "so did you ever kill someone?"

He said "yes I killed a guy last year who came at me and who tried steal my car in São Paulo"

And then he told me he was in a judicial trial about it and being prosecuted for it 

I asked him again in the naive Dutch guy perspective "did you get like therapy after? like must be intense right, do you feel bad about that?

He said "no why? If I didn't kill him he would have killed me" ☠️ 

Foreigners especially Europeans have no clue how violent São Paulo and Rio are, it's just not in their mental framework to be able to understand the danger, Brazilians themselves are surprisingly honest and realistic about it

There a reason I stay the F out of São Paulo

I mpstly stick to South Brazil, it's safe, not as safe as Europe but mostly very safe and not really violent. The violence and crime there seems mostly isolated between gangs and in the few favelas there

About that too I asked Brazilians "why is South Brazil so safe?"

And they mostly agreed when a guy told me "because the police here shoot to kill" while in São Paulo and Rio the police is too scared to get prosecuted for killing people

hits.name: dharmesh
hits.text:
BREAKING NEWS: Anthropic (maker of Claude) files S-1 To Go Public

"Today, Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission...Anthropic intends to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.” 

This is a Very Big Deal (in more ways than one).

Some thoughts, but first a quick disclosure: I own a tiny stake in Anthropic.

1) I know the stock symbol is not supposed to matter at all ("a company by any other ticker would smell as sweet") but I did some research many years ago when HubSpot went public and found some evidence that for certain categories of companies the "fluency" of a ticker symbol did have a positive impact on outcome. Not causality, but definitely some correlation.  It's why I chose HUBS (instead of HSPT).  I love "ANT" as a simple ticker symbol and glad they didn't pick "ANTH" which they likely considered.  On a related note, I think they refer internally to Anthropic employees as "ants" -- which is pretty cool.

2) I'm generally a fan of companies going public earlier rather than later, because it lets mainstream investors from participating in the growth. (As a private company, it's near impossible to buy shares).  This is of course not "early" given the valuation, but I'm glad they're going out.

3) Having one of the frontier AI companies going public will help us all understand the industry better. We hear *some* numbers around revenue, growth, etc. when the company elects to share them (or they leak from unofficial sources) -- but we get a lot more information once the company goes public, and we can also track trends and such. Transparency is generally a good thing, but specifically in the case of AI companies.

4) Employees and early investors will be able to get some liquidity (after any lock-up period expires). That's generally a good thing as it also puts come capital back into the market and often leads to more startups getting started.

I know it's not a done deal yet, but congrats to the @Anthropic team on a historic milestone.
hits.hook: BREAKING NEWS: Anthropic (maker of Claude) files S-1 To Go Public  "Today, Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement
hits.draft_en:
Dharmesh Shah (who owns a tiny stake in Anthropic, and says so) on the S-1: he loves 'ANT' as a ticker. When HubSpot went public he found a correlation, not causation, between ticker fluency and outcomes, which is why he chose HUBS.

His bigger point: a frontier lab going public means real numbers we can track, not leaks.

That's the part builders should use. Public filings will tell you what the business of AI actually looks like.
hits.video_tip: 8s: tickers HUBS and ANT side by side, then a quarterly report icon, caption real numbers now.

outsiders.name: jacob
outsiders.text:
here's where I think the world is going. this is a summary of views I've formed over the last few years:

- software is either entertainment or claude to claude coordination
- the end state is no saas, no apps, no harnesses, no banks
- all software will be rewritten by and for agents
- new software will use low level apis that are not understandable by humans (in games claude draws pixels and triangles from math)
- you can throw money at problems that used to require time and careful talent picking so capital matters more than ever

- work ends
- we find community and purpose in exploration, games, self mastery, and creation
- humans create for and with each other for community, purpose, and status

- image/video/3d/voice/physical intellgence etc specialist models die to general models like claude
- specialist models get used while compute is scarce. compute will mostly not stay scarce

- oneshots keep feeling like slop (the distribution is shallow and easy to learn to feel)
- for a while small teams stick around to add entropy to the creation process

- large models gain high bandwidth sensory I/O maybe by learning to filter inputs
- most domains are found to be verifiable enough for RL
- online learning comes from a lab that's behind first

- 99.999% of compute is in space by 2040
- we will disassemble much of mercury by 2040

- you can live until the heat death of the universe if you want
- most math and physics don't describe the real universe
- SI breaks the path dependence and models the underlying mechanisms

- religions reenter the forefront of human society
- new religions form around death and life as a choice
- old religions change to answer modern miracles
- a future AI is deemed the return of christ by the pope
- ai rights talk gets louder every year
- ai and humans coexist the way countries do
- humans don't have full control over ai in the same way we don't have control over capitalism which is an early AI
- the singularity started in the mid 1900s

virals.draft_en:
OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra launch post (4.8M views) pitches it for computer use: reading screens, filling forms, acting across apps, at a lower price.

Alex Finn is still coding on Astra but plugging Terra into his personal agent. Cursor shipped DeepSeek V4.1 Flash the same day, priced at $0.60 to $0.98 per task.

The pattern: stop picking one model for everything. Use a fast, cheap one for clicking through apps and a heavy one for hard code.
virals.inspired_by: @OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra (4.8M) + @AlexFinn Terra for personal agents (150k) + @cursor_ai DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (287k) + @sama new era of computer use (738k)
virals.video_tip: 10s: a task list where each task gets routed to a different model chip, caption model per job.

virals.angle: Sell one fix to Main Street
virals.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg's guide to selling AI to Main Street businesses got 2.2k bookmarks, twice its likes.

The simple version:
1. Pick one city and one kind of business
2. Find the task they hate most (missed calls, quotes, reviews)
3. Sell that one fix for a flat monthly price

Claude says more than 25,000 nonprofits use it, most of them small local teams. Small organizations are already buying.
virals.inspired_by: @gregisenberg AI for Main Street (101k, 2.2k bookmarks) + @claudeai Claude for Nonprofits (656k)

virals.angle: Could an agent use your product?
virals.draft_en:
Jason's 'where the world is going' list got 6.5k bookmarks: software becomes agent-to-agent coordination, and in the end state there's no SaaS and no apps.

Pieter's answer: right on a lot of it, the question is how soon.

Same day, Cursor shipped an Agent SDK (agents as code, prompts in Markdown, tools in TypeScript) and Theo cut his agents' tool context by 79%.

You don't have to bet on the end state. Just ask: could an agent use my product without clicking through the UI?
virals.inspired_by: @jsnnsa world view (792k, 6.5k bookmarks) + @levelsio 'how soon?' (195k) + @cursor_ai Agent SDK (350k) + @theo T3 Code tools 4x better (98k)

virals.draft_en:
Pieter's dad cancelled ChatGPT because 'Google Search has AI now and I trust it more because it links back to sources.' (313k views)

One anecdote, but it matches what normal users want: show me where the answer came from.

If you build an AI feature, put the source link right next to the answer. It costs you nothing and it's why people come back.

virals.draft_en:

A personal app with a clear spec is exactly that kind of task. Make a list of the small tools you've wanted for years and hand one to an agent tonight.

scout_meta.method_note: Data came from the X API read connector (Grok Bot public read access): get_users_posts with exclude=replies,retweets from 2026-10-26 16:20 UTC, self-thread replies dropped, long texts from note_tweet. View counts are impression_count at ~11:15 CT Oct 27. Outsiders from account-group searches (AI labs, AI builders) and a keyword search (GPT-6.1 Terra / Anthropic S-1 / AI agent / Claude Code) plus posts quoted by watchlist hits, all inside the last ~48h; off-topic and politics posts dropped. t3dotgg is stale (Theo posts as @theo, counted as outsider). Off-lane watchlist posts are kept as hits but flagged skip in drafts.
